dedupe_keys.name: state dependent tsunami fragility functions via ad hoc scaling factors riesgos pacific coast of south america

description: This data publication provides tsunami fragility functions for building classes on the Pacific coast of South America, extended into state-dependent fragility functions that account for damage already caused by a preceding earthquake. It was published in 2022 on GFZ Data Services by Juan Camilo Gomez-Zapata, Sergio Medina and Juan Lizarazo-Marriaga within the RIESGOS project, which built multi-hazard risk information services for the Andes. It describes the building classification scheme for tsunami vulnerability and the flow-depth-based analytical fragility functions proposed by Medina (2019), and derives state-dependent versions by applying scaling factors obtained as ad-hoc calibration parameters; a Python script, its inputs and resulting model files are included. Coverage is the building classes of coastal Peru and neighbouring countries studied in RIESGOS. Access: open download from GFZ Data Services. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the scaling factors are ad hoc, not fitted to observed sequential damage. Simulation uses are cumulative earthquake-then-tsunami damage modelling in multi-hazard risk chains. Related records: the collapse volume ratio fatality data and IN-CORE fragility libraries.
